title: Per-tenant SLO matrix and automated traffic-shift guardrails
creator: Samira Chen
description: PRD to define a per-tenant SLO matrix (Premium, Standard, Bulk) and an automated traffic-shift gating system for model rollouts. This ticket captures explicit latency and availability targets, error-budget accounting rules per tenant class, alerting thresholds, and the automated heuristics that will stop/rollback traffic shifts when risk thresholds are exceeded.
background: We currently operate a single global SLO for hosted endpoints which masks variability across high-priority customers and large-volume tenants. This has led to manual rollbacks and customer escalations during rollouts. The goal is to provide deterministic guardrails that allow safe progressive traffic shifts while protecting higher-tier customers and limiting blast radius.
goals: Define measurable SLOs for three tenant classes: Premium, Standard, Bulk
Specify error budget calculation and burn-rate windows per tenant
Design automated traffic-shift schedule and stop/rollback heuristics
Create console dashboards and per-tenant alerting for SRE/PM/Account teams
Provide acceptance criteria and playbooks for on-call and SEs
scope: Define SLO targets, error budget math, rollout percentages and timing, guard conditions for pause/rollback, dashboard requirements, and alerting runbooks. Implement gating config in rollout service and add observability wiring. No code-level runtime kernel changes are in scope for this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: SLO matrix documented and approved by SRE, Infra, and Sales Engineering
Rollout service accepts per-tenant guard config and enforces stops/rollbacks automatically
Console shows live per-tenant error budget, burn rate, and traffic shift status
Alerts fire to on-call when any guard condition is met and include remediation steps
Playbook with step-by-step rollback and customer communication templates is published
alert_thresholds: Immediate P95 breach: if P95 > target by >20% for 5m for Premium => pause traffic shift
Sustained P95 breach: if P95 > target for 15m across >50% of Premium shards => pause and rollback
Error budget burn: if >30% of error budget consumed in 1h for any tenant => pause further ramps
Rapid burn rate: if burn rate >5x expected over 30m => immediate rollback
Availability drop: if availability falls below target - 0.2% for 10m => stop rollout
rollout_strategy: Progressive ramps by tenant class: start with 1% of non-production traffic, then 10%, 25%, 50%, 100
Prioritize Premium tenants for conservative ramps (10% -> 25% -> 50% with longer observation windows)
Apply canary windows: default observation windows are 15m at 10%, 30m at 25%, 1h at 50%
Parallel rollouts to Bulk class must run in isolated capacity pools where possible
Auto-rollback triggers are evaluated continuously and can be overridden only by two SRE approvals
rollback_gates: Immediate automatic rollback when any Premium tenant triggers an immediate P95 breach condition
Automatic rollback when error budget consumption exceeds 80% in a 24h window for a tenant class
Manual hold (requires SRE + PM approval) if burn is between 50%-80% and customer-impact is medium
Soft-degrade step: if non-critical regressions are detected, route Premium to fallback model variant while continuing limited rollout to Standard
operational_playbook: Runbook link: Confluence -> Per-tenant SLOs and Rollout Playbook
On-call steps: verify metrics, confirm automated rollback logs, notify SE and account owner
Customer comms template for incident and rollback notifications
Postmortem checklist: collect traces, top tokens, model outputs, and recent config changes
notes: Open decisions: exact burn-rate multipliers for Bulk class (tradeoff: availability vs. cost), whether to auto-notify account owners on pause vs only on rollback, and retention window for per-tenant SLO history. Implementation should be incremental: start with Premium+Standard then add Bulk after 2 weeks of stable telemetry. Ensure feature flagging for controlled rollout to internal customers first.
